name: The Farm at San Benito, Autograph Collection
short_description: An Autograph Collection wellness resort on 52 hectares in Lipa, Batangas, pairing a holistic medical spa, plant-based farm-to-table dining, and garden villas about two hours south of Manila.
ai_summary: The Farm at San Benito is an eco-luxury holistic wellness resort that joined Marriott's Autograph Collection in 2025 after more than two decades operating independently. Set on 52 hectares of tropical forest and gardens in Lipa City, Batangas, it centers on an integrated medical wellness program: onsite doctors, diagnostics, nutritional guidance, detox and cleanse protocols, and the multi-sanctuary Healing Spa with pools, flotation pods, infrared sauna, and thermal therapies. Reviewers across independent travel and wellness publications consistently praise the serene setting, warm and professional staff, and surprisingly delicious award-winning plant-based, farm-to-table cuisine, much of it grown onsite and served across restaurants including Alive!, Pesce, and SoufflE de Vie. Villas range from garden and pool villas to large luxury residences with private pools. Guests describe it as a genuinely restorative reset rather than a clinical facility, with abundant complimentary yoga, meditation, sound healing, and guided activities. Honest watch-outs recur: the strict detox programs can leave non-weight-loss guests hungry, the jungle setting means insects and wildlife, some older room categories such as the Palmera suites feel cramped, and pricing is firmly premium and not budget-friendly. As a wellness-first, multi-night destination with vegan-forward dining, it suits travelers seeking health-focused relaxation more than a conventional short city or beach stay. TripAdvisor ranks it #1 of the hotels in Lipa City with a 4.5 aggregate rating.

faqs.question: Where is The Farm at San Benito and how do I get there?
faqs.answer: It sits on 52 hectares in Barangay Tipacan, Lipa City, Batangas, roughly 90 kilometers and about a two-hour drive south of Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila. Most guests arrange a private transfer, since there is no convenient public transport to the resort itself.

faqs.question: What kind of resort is The Farm at San Benito?
faqs.answer: It is a holistic medical wellness resort, not a conventional hotel. Guests typically book multi-night programs combining doctor-led diagnostics, detox and cleanse protocols, spa therapies, yoga and meditation, and plant-based farm-to-table dining, all set within tropical gardens designed for rest and recovery.

faqs.question: Is the food really all plant-based?
faqs.answer: Yes, dining is vegan and largely grown onsite, served across restaurants such as Alive!, Pesce, and SoufflE de Vie. Reviewers consistently report the cuisine is flavorful and satisfying, though guests who prefer meat or are traveling with non-participants should plan for the fully plant-based menus.

reviews.title: Hotel Review: Why The Farm at San Benito is the ideal wellness escape in the Philippines
reviews.author: Dudi Aureus
reviews.summary: Praises the 52-hectare forest setting, warm hospitality, and medical wellness center; highlights the Mahogany luxury residence, signature Hilot massage, and five farm-to-table restaurants serving organic vegan cuisine.

reviews.title: The Farm at San Benito: The Best Eco-Luxury Medical Wellness Resort in Asia
reviews.author: Nam Cheah
reviews.summary: Calls it one of the best resorts stayed at, praising the fairy-tale infinity pool, 600-year-old mango tree, and delicious vegan food; notes yoga can feel too gentle and the property is not cheap.

reviews.title: An Indulgent Five-Star Detox At The Farm At San Benito
reviews.author: Natalie Soderstrom
reviews.summary: Highlights personalized programming, award-winning plant-based cuisine, and three spa sanctuaries in a serene jungle setting; warns of occasional hunger on strict detox and jungle wildlife like bugs and toads.

reviews.title: Farm at San Benito, a resort review
reviews.author: Anita Sane
reviews.summary: Rates it a first-class 4/5 retreat with excellent vegan food, attentive staff, and many complimentary activities; flags cramped Palmera suites, no public transport, high restaurant pricing, and a multi-night focus.

reviews.title: Samantha's Review of The Farm at San Benito
reviews.author: Lisa Haidacher
reviews.summary: Praises the detailed health assessment, jungle-gym fitness and varied yoga classes, gourmet vegan dining at Alive!, and the Narra pool villa with private heated pool; notes the personalized wellness programming.
